My research connects nanoscale process development and heterogeneous materials integration with single-molecule measurement. I study how fabrication, pore geometry, material interfaces, and molecular structure influence transport and ionic-current signals in solid-state and hybrid nanopores.

## Current research

### α-Hemolysin hybrid nanopores (2026–present)

I lead ongoing work on integrating α-hemolysin with quartz nanopipettes for single-molecule sensing. My work focuses on electrical characterization and device stability.
### Programmable nanopore fabrication (2026–present)

I co-developed P.O.R.E., a low-cost programmable system for fabricating solid-state nanopores. I led the mechanical and microfluidic design, built flow-cell cartridges, assembled the system, and validated its performance experimentally. [Project details](projects/instrumentation.qmd).
### Multiphysics modeling and machine learning

Electric-field simulations and event-level signal analysis help relate device architecture to transport behavior and support classification of experimental signals. [Project details](projects/modeling-ml.qmd).
## Completed and published research

### Multilayer heterostructure nanopores (2025–2026)

I co-led work on silicon nitride nanopores incorporating graphene, MoS₂, and hBN using the lab’s existing chemically tuned controlled dielectric breakdown method. I investigated how these interfaces affect protein transport and current blockades, and used Gaussian mixture models and ensemble classification to analyze translocation signals. [Project details](projects/heterostructures.qmd).
### Collaborative sensing studies

I contributed nanopore measurements and data analysis to studies of [dendrimer–peptide conjugates](https://doi.org/10.1002/admi.70569), [ferritin subunits](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.nanolett.6c00914), and [ultra-short peptides](https://doi.org/10.1002/elps.8122).

### DNA-templated silver nanoclusters (2024–2025)

I co-led nanopore and fluorescence characterization of DNA-templated silver nanoclusters. Our published work found distinct electrical signatures for DNA templates with and without silver nanoclusters under electrolyte conditions that stabilize the clusters. [Project details](projects/silver-nanoclusters.qmd).
### DNA origami hybrid nanopores (2023–2024)

I led experiments incorporating three-dimensional DNA origami into silicon nitride nanopores. I studied trapping stability and ionic-current responses during protein transport. In our published study, the hybrid device improved sensitivity for detecting holo-human serum transferrin. [Project details](projects/dna-origami.qmd).
## Earlier research

At SEGi University, I used ANSYS Fluent to compare forward- and backward-swept C-wing configurations at supersonic speeds. This work received the IMechE Project Award. I also co-authored a [review of 3D printing in orthopedic surgery](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0165255).

## Research techniques and skills

| Area | Techniques and tools |
|:--|:--|
| Nanofabrication | Solid-state nanopore and quartz nanopipette fabrication, controlled dielectric breakdown, 2D-material transfer, and heterogeneous membrane integration |
| Characterization | Ionic-current and current–voltage measurements, SEM/EDX, AFM, Raman, UV–Vis, and fluorescence spectroscopy |
| Instrumentation and prototyping | Axopatch/Digidata, Sutter P-2000, microfluidic flow-cell design, CAD, 3D printing, and Arduino-based instrumentation |
| Signal processing and statistics | Single-molecule event detection, current blockade and dwell-time analysis, power spectral density, signal-to-noise ratios, ANOVA, and effect sizes |
| Computation and machine learning | Python, MATLAB, and COMSOL Multiphysics; Gaussian mixture models, ensemble classification, and model interpretation with SHAP |
| Semiconductor processing coursework | Photolithography, oxidation, doping, etching, and metallization |
